name: Hotspot Layer
description: The regions of a scene that answer when you click them, and the cursor that tells you so before you do. A hotspot carries a shape, a set of verbs it accepts and a state, and the cursor is derived from the verbs rather than set by hand — a scene where the cursor and the accepted verb disagree is a scene that lies about what is possible. Pixel-hunting is the genre's oldest failure, so a highlight-all key is an input rather than an accessibility afterthought. Hotspots go stale: one that has given up everything it holds reports itself exhausted, which is what lets a room tell a stuck player they have already found everything here.

inputs.name: hotspots
inputs.description: Regions with their shapes, accepted verbs and initial states. Required — the scene is content.

inputs.name: cursorByVerb
inputs.description: Cursor shown per accepted verb, so the pointer never contradicts what is possible.

inputs.name: highlightAllKey
inputs.description: Whether a key reveals every hotspot at once. The direct answer to pixel-hunting.

inputs.name: reportExhausted
inputs.description: Whether a hotspot that has nothing left to give says so, so a stuck player is not re-searching solved ground.

outputs.name: activeHotspot
outputs.description: The region under the cursor, or null.

outputs.name: exhausted
outputs.description: Hotspot ids with nothing left to give.

outputs.name: cursor
outputs.description: Cursor implied by the active hotspot's verbs.
